title: India’s first dengue vaccine arrives with a crucial safety caveat
summary: India has approved Qdenga, the country’s first dengue vaccine, for people aged 4–60. The vaccine targets all four dengue serotypes and is already authorized in over 40 countries. However, phase-3 trial data published by manufacturer Takeda raise specific safety and efficacy concerns that regulators and clinicians must weigh before broad rollout.
content:
Updated - July 27, 2026 10:59 am IST

The efficacy and safety of a dengue vaccine are linked to each other as two sides of the same coin, and Qdenga’s phase-3 trial data need to be understood through this lens.

India’s drug regulator has approved the country’s first dengue vaccine, Qdenga. The vaccine is designed and claimed to protect against the four serotypes of the dengue-causing virus, DENV-1 to DENV-4.

Qdenga is indicated for children and adults aged 4 to 60 years, and the approval allows vaccination irrespective of whether recipients have had dengue previously. This broad age range and the absence of a prior-infection requirement make the vaccine potentially useful for large-scale public health programs.

More than 40 countries have already approved Qdenga. It is manufactured by the Japanese pharmaceutical company Takeda. That global rollout and experience informed regulatory review in India.

However, data from clinical trials that Takeda published in 2019, 2020 and 2024 on the vaccine’s efficacy raise a specific concern about its performance and safety profile in certain groups. Observers and public health officials note that efficacy and safety outcomes must be interpreted together to assess net benefit.

Indian clinicians and policymakers will need to consider the phase-3 trial findings carefully when planning vaccination strategies, particularly around age groups, surveillance for adverse events, and communication with the public. Further post-approval monitoring and transparent data sharing will be important to ensure the vaccine’s benefits outweigh risks in India’s diverse population.

Published - July 27, 2026 09:00 am IST
